<b>Chaque usine est en mode simple ou en: Every factory is in simple mode or in faithful mode, and the setting lives in the document, not in the preferences: a factory you share opens on the other side in the mode it was thought out in, or the figures would change. Simple mode — what a new factory starts in — lets a port carry as many lines as you like and splits evenly between them; it is the mode for thinking about rates. Faithful mode applies the game's own rule, one port one line, and makes you place the fittings; it is the mode for building. The Fittings menu switches, and the switch can be undone.
<b>Filtrer sur un objet ne change rien,: Filtering on an item changes nothing here. A line carries one item: filtering a branch on the item it already carries amounts to "any", and filtering it on another one closes it completely — which is reported. Setting filters and expecting the rates to move will do nothing; what you want is overflow. And the game filters conveyors only: there is no smart pipeline junction.
<b>Générer une usine</b> développe une c: Generate a factory expands a target — "two Heavy Modular Frames a minute" — into machines, lines and fittings, by the standard recipe except where you pin another one. Two variants: exact ratios, with machines at a decimal count, or rounded up to whole buildings, buildable as it stands, with a container wherever the rounding leaves a surplus. What comes out is an ordinary factory, editable at once.
<b>Indicatif.</b> Le calcul ne suit que: Rough guide. The figures follow standard recipes only and credit no byproducts: one alternate recipe, or one byproduct sold, changes the answer. For an exact number, build the factory.
<b>L'azote ne sort du sol que par un pui: Nitrogen Gas comes out of the ground through a resource well and nothing else: no miner and no pump works it, it is a raw resource in gas form. Place a well, and Nitric Acid, the Cooling System, the Fused Modular Frame and Rocket Fuel become buildable end to end.
<b>La capacité d'une ligne est une contr: The capacity of a line is a constraint, not a remark. A Conveyor Belt Mk.1 fed 480/min carries 60 and backs the rest up. The finding gives both figures — carried and demanded — because it is the second one that names the tier to install, and it is computed by a twin solve with no ceiling rather than estimated.
<b>La centrale nucléaire produit sur une: The Nuclear Power Plant produces onto a belt, and it is the only generator in the game that does. It returns 50 Uranium Waste per fuel rod — 10 a minute — and 10 Plutonium Waste per Plutonium Fuel Rod; a Ficsonium Fuel Rod leaves nothing. So the byproduct rule applies to it: a plant whose waste goes nowhere stops, exactly as a refinery does, and stops producing a single megawatt. Its make-up water is considerable: 240 m³/min, against 45 for a Coal-Powered Generator.
<b>La liste de courses compte les raccor: The shopping list counts fittings in both modes, and not the same way. In simple mode they are deduced: four lines on one port need two of them, in the thriftiest chain. In faithful mode they are counted where they are placed, and a factory drawn by hand often uses more — a tree built for symmetry, a fitting left standing after a machine count came down. A total that goes up when you switch is therefore not an inconsistency: it is the drawing saying something the deduction had no way of knowing.
<b>Le brûleur de biomasse n'a pas de cha: The Biomass Burner has no supply chain, and that is not an oversight. Biomass is crafted by hand in the game, out of wood, leaves or Mycelia you pick up: no machine makes it, so no recipe can make it here. Feed it from an outside supply at the rate you undertake to keep up. The same goes for everything downstream of biomass — Solid Biofuel, then Liquid Biofuel. That, along with alien remains, is all that stays out of the catalogue's reach: gathering, and nothing else.
<b>Le générateur géothermique ne brûle r: The Geothermal Generator burns nothing: it sits on a geyser, and the geyser's purity decides. The game itself announces 100, 300 or 600 MW at peak depending on the geyser; since this model is a steady state, what is counted is the average — 100, 200 or 400 MW. The purity is something you enter, as a deposit's is, because nothing in the game data says where the geysers on your map are. It cannot be overclocked: the game refuses, for this generator alone.
<b>Le nombre de machines est ce que vous: The machine count is what you enter, never what the tool decides. Beside it, the tool tells you how many are actually useful given what arrives, and the gap between the two. To take the problem from the other end — "I want this much a minute" — use Generate a factory.
<b>Le partage est max-min, pas proportio: Splitting is max-min, not proportional. Every branch gets an equal share, and whatever a saturated branch cannot take is shared out equally among the others: 60 ingots for two consumers asking for 30 and 60 give 30 and 30 — the smaller one is served in full — and not 20 and 40, which would leave both limping. And a real tree only splits evenly when the number of branches comes down to halves and thirds: 2, 3, 4, 6 and 9 yes, 5 and 7 no. That is how the game is.
<b>Toutes les machines du jeu sont au ca: Every machine in the game is in the catalogue, and the 291 recipes they make can all be placed. What stays out are the 26 hand-crafted recipes of the Equipment Workshop — parachute, chainsaw, rifle: a workshop will never be a factory node. An item's card shows them greyed and without a button to place them, and says why. And an item no recipe in the game produces says where it comes from: picked up in the world, or a byproduct — Uranium Waste comes out of the Nuclear Power Plant, ten a minute, it is not picked up anywhere. An absence that does not name itself reads as a hole in the data.
<b>Trois machines consomment selon ce qu: Three machines draw power according to what they make, not according to what they are: the Converter, the Particle Accelerator and the Quantum Encoder. Their nameplate is zero and the figure is carried by the recipe. In game their draw swings — the Accelerator runs 250 to 750 MW on Diamonds, 500 to 1500 on Dark Matter; the Encoder, 0 to 2000 — and since this model is a steady state, what is counted is the average, the middle of the swing. The item card shows both ends beside it, because sizing a power plant on an Encoder's average without knowing it touches two gigawatts would be an unpleasant surprise.
<b>Un port porte une ligne</b> en mode f: A port carries one line in faithful mode, and a node has as many ports as it has buildings: eight Smelters have eight outputs, one has one. To run more lines out, place a splitter — it is a node like any other, it splits evenly between its branches and it is counted in the shopping list. A factory import and a factory export are the boundary of the model and not buildings: they have no limit.
<b>Un puits de ressource est deux bâtime: A resource well is two buildings, and only one of them draws power. The pressurizer costs 150 MW, one of them whatever the number of satellites; the satellites themselves draw nothing. An empty well therefore already costs its 150 MW, which is reported. Each satellite gives 30, 60 or 120 m³/min depending on its purity and carries its own pipe: three satellites make three output ports. Overclocking acts on the whole well — the rate follows, and the bill follows the pressurizer's exponent.
<b>Un sous-produit sans issue arrête la: A byproduct with nowhere to go stops the machine completely. A recipe that makes two things has to see both leave: without that the node falls to 0%, as in game where the machine clogs. This blockage is judged on the topology and not on the rate — an output that only absorbs part of it does not block, it applies back pressure and the operating rate comes down.
<b>Une machine à l'arrêt consomme quand: A stopped machine draws power all the same. Production follows the operating rate, consumption does not: a blocked or starved node pays its bill in full, as in game. Nobody noticed at 4 MW; everybody notices with a blocked Quantum Encoder, which is this catalogue's most expensive way of producing nothing.
<b>{missing} MW manquants.</b> Ce défici: {missing} MW short. This shortfall throttles none of the rates above: in game, running out of power does not slow the factory down, it trips the whole grid until someone switches it back on.

L'électricité est un <b>compteur, pas un: Electricity is a counter, not a constraint: consumption and production are shown side by side, and a shortfall throttles no rate. In game, running out of power does not slow the factory down, it trips the whole grid until someone intervenes; showing everything at zero would teach nothing, and throttling part of it would be an invention. Generators themselves run at 100%: their overclocking follows a different exponent from the machines' and will be work of its own.
La branche vers {branch} est filtrée sur: The branch to {branch} filters on {wanted}, which this line never carries: it carries {carried}. Nothing will go that way.
La cadence multiplie le débit à l'identi: The clock multiplies the rate one for one and the power by a power law: at 250%, a machine produces 2.5 times as much and draws about 3.36 times as much. The exponent is the same for every production machine, including the three below.
La consommation compte les machines <b>à: Consumption counts stopped machines: they are built and plugged in. This is worst-case sizing, not a measurement of the game — the files declare no idle draw, only a nominal one, and inventing a reduced figure would be worse than counting the maximum. Production, on the other hand, counts only what actually burns: a generator with no fuel produces nothing.
La pureté d'un gisement s'applique à <b>: A deposit's purity applies to every extractor on that node: a node is a deposit. Two deposits of different purities are two nodes, and that is the only way to represent them. A geyser reads the same way, with geothermal generators in place of extractors. The rule holds for a deposit, not for a resource well: a pressurizer opens several satellites at once and nothing says they match, so there the purity is per satellite and the node carries a tally — "1 impure · 2 normal · 3 pure" — instead of one value. Keeping the deposit rule whole is precisely why a well is a node kind of its own.
